text:
eve_sales: Quick sync: MedData POC needs Private/VPC connectivity for calling our private inference endpoint from their on-prem EHR cluster. They asked for a clear recommendation: PrivateLink vs VPC peering/TGW, a minimal firewall allowlist snippet, and whether we can offer a single static IP for allowlisting. Who can advise?
lina_netops: Short: PrivateLink = easiest to get through security audits (service scoped, no route table surgery). Peering/TGW = full L3, preserves client source IPs, better if they need transparent client IPs for logging.
kevin_ae: PrivateLink mechanics to highlight: customer creates an Interface Endpoint in their VPC referencing our service name OR we publish a service and they create it — either way the ENIs live in their subnets and have private IPs. If they create the endpoint in their account, allowlisting is straightforward (use the ENI IPs).
omar_solutions: For a fast POC I usually ask customers to create the interface endpoint in their VPC and put the endpoint in a private subnet. That avoids cross-account routing changes and keeps blast radius small.
julia_sec: Security checks: confirm whether MedData will do TLS inspection. If they do, cert pinning can break. Recommend token-based auth or mTLS for the POC if they insist on inspection. Also request VPC Flow Logs on the endpoint subnets for auditability.
eve_sales: They only allow outbound 443 from their EHR cluster. Is that okay for PrivateLink/peering?
lina_netops: Yes — 443/tcp is sufficient. PrivateLink traffic is still TLS. If you choose peering and they egress via our public endpoints, you'd need to allow our public NAT EIP(s) instead.
kevin_ae: One-line allowlist example (give to their netsec):
```
allow tcp from 10.12.0.0/20 to 10.240.10.0/28 port 443  # replace dest CIDR with actual endpoint ENIs
```
And a concise single-IP option if they require it:
```
allow tcp from 10.12.0.0/20 to 54.216.33.77 port 443  # example dedicated EIP (if we provision a proxy/NAT)
```
omar_solutions: Notes on the single-IP approach: we can provision a dedicated proxy/NAT with a customer-dedicated EIP, but that adds setup effort (infra ticket) and a small monthly infra surcharge. It also forces traffic over public egress unless you colocate the proxy in their VPC.
julia_sec: Compliance caveat: if we supply a shared IP, it must be single-tenant for customers with strict audits. Don't share EIPs across customers.
eve_sales: How about pricing delta for PrivateLink vs TGW? POC-level estimate is fine.
kevin_ae: High level: PrivateLink -> per-hour endpoint charges + per-GB processing on cloud provider side (they usually pay these). TGW/transit -> per-hour attachment + per-GB transit on provider; TGW can be cheaper for heavy sustained throughput but slower to approve. If we provide an EIP/proxy we bill a flat setup + monthly infra fee + per-GB handling.
mar: (typo fix)
omar_solutions: Operational gotcha: interface endpoints create ENIs in multiple AZs; make sure their subnet quotas allow it. Also test MTU for streaming — some paths with inspection/proxies lower MTU and can break gRPC/streaming.
kevin_ae: DNS: PrivateLink endpoints often resolve to regional private IPs via the AWS private DNS name; confirm their DNS will resolve the endpoint name to the ENI IPs. If they use host-based allowlists, provide ENI CIDRs; if they rely on FQDN-only allowlisting, confirm proxy behavior.
eve_sales: Great. Can someone draft 2-3 sentence bullets I can email the customer?
omar_solutions: Email bullets: 
- PrivateLink (recommended for POC): minimal routing changes, supports endpoint policies, customer can create interface endpoint and allowlist ENI IPs; quick approval for security teams.
- VPC Peering / Transit: full L3, preserves client source IPs and is best for long-term integrations; requires route updates and change windows.
- Dedicated EIP / Proxy: single-IP allowlist for strict firewalls; requires provisioning and incurs infra/setup + monthly fee.
Next steps: confirm (1) cloud provider + region, (2) whether MedData will accept ENI CIDR allowlist or requires single EIP, (3) whether TLS inspection is in scope. We'll open infra ticket once they confirm.

eve_sales: Thanks all, will send email and push for region info :pray:
